LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION MARKS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which punctuation marks do you know?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences
2. punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 9.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION MARKS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 9.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION MARKS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark

What this means
In this part you learn to punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks to a partner. (skill: punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences.
3. Practise this skill: punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which punctuation marks do you know?
2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the apostrophe and exclamation mark in sentences.
5. Be able to: punctuate sentences correctly using the apostrophe and the exclamation mark.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
